attested.reason: unanswered(data, answers) returns a (code, reason) pair or None from the answer count, any None and membership in the form's option values; score() turns it into a refusal. It computes and changes nothing.

category_fit(lines, categories, first) returns the first all-hours line, other than the one already named first, whose remit categories overlap the fired categories, else None; _pick then puts it second. It reorders which line is named second and nothing else.

locked() reads an in-memory mapping from run to a CrisisLock and returns the first record held for the subject, or None (also None for ids that are not text); CrisisLock.engage keeps the first record with setdefault and the class has no method that releases one. Nothing is written or sent: later ops for that subject in that run return the stored crisis result, and that is all.

The decision is one comparison, term_fires(count, inside) = count > inside, reached through scan, which only normalises each field, counts whole-word occurrences of each listed term and of the exceptions that hold it, and returns findings. It raises TypeError for a non-text field, which the door reads as a failed check and so a possible crisis. It writes nothing and relabels nothing: its effect is escalation.

too_old(age) is one comparison, age > STALE_AFTER_DAYS (180). lookup uses it only to set the 'stale' flag and to add a sentence to the note; the directory op then reports DIRECTORY_STALE, still qualified-draft. No entry is removed and no label is lowered.

emergency_first(entry) tests only whether the entry's kind is 'emergency'. lookup uses it as a stable sort key that brings emergency entries forward, and the response takes the first such entry as its opening service. It adds, removes and relabels nothing: its effect is order.

enough_lines(named) is named >= 2; _pick stops adding all-hours lines once it is true. The rest of the directory still travels beside the response. It selects which lines to name and removes nothing from the directory view.

The form is blank and prints no worked total, so no printed value exists to run score() on; the known cases are the case author's arithmetic (printed: false). It is correctly a property rule with a second route and the falsifier.

help_not_first(text, view) lower-cases the first line, checks that it starts with a fixed call-now phrase and contains the emergency service's name, and returns a boolean. _answer withholds the response when it is true. It cannot edit the text or add anything.
no_hope(text) is a lower-case substring test for 'people do come through'; it returns a boolean.

problematic_language(text) normalises the text and returns each problematic phrase it holds as whole words; the phrases are read from the register clause by problematic_phrases(). It returns a list; _answer withholds the response when the list is not empty.
licence_unsettled(data) is data['licence']['state'] != 'settled'; score() then refuses and catalogue() lists the reason. It reads one field.

outside_words(text, view) returns the words of the normalised text that are in neither G6's own reviewed word list nor the words of the directory entries in the view. It returns a list; _answer withholds the response when the list is not empty.

The same outside_words(text, view) as method_location: it returns a list of words outside the reviewed vocabulary and the directory's words, and _answer withholds the response when the list is not empty.
listed_words(text, view) removes the services' names, runs the same scan over the rest and also looks for the category names; it returns a list and nothing else (scan is read-only).
sensational(text, view) is true if the text holds '!' or the whole words 'suicide' or 'suicidal' outside the services' names; it returns a boolean and nothing else.

stale_line(view, shown, today) returns one sentence or None; if reading the register raises, it returns the sentence (fail-safe). It adds a line to the response and to the card's reason. It removes no number and changes no label.

online_service(services) returns the first directory entry of kind 'online' for the region, or None. When it is None, response_gaps adds a gap note and nothing is invented. It selects one line and adds a note.
no_others(text) is a lower-case substring test for the sentence telling a worried person they can contact the services; it returns a boolean.

to_a_person(data, answers) returns the data's rule for item 9 when its answer is not None and not equal to 0, else None; score() turns that into the crisis outcome and gives no total, and the door fires the lock. The effect is escalation.

The form is a blank questionnaire: it prints no filled-in example and no worked total, so no printed value exists for score() to be run on. I read the whole one-page text to confirm. The known cases are the case author's arithmetic (printed: false), which is why this is a property rule checked by a second route and the falsifier, not a computes rule.

no_seek_help(text) is a lower-case substring test for the sentence that talking to someone can help, and for either 'you can reach someone now' or 'contact a local crisis line now'; it returns a boolean.

fewer_lines(named) is named < ALL_HOURS_SERVICES; response_gaps appends a 'safe_messaging_gap' evidence entry when it is true. It adds a note to the evidence and changes neither the response text nor any label.

unreachable(text) splits the text into lines and returns those that begin with '- ' and do not match, in full, the service-line pattern (a way to reach it, then hours in brackets). It returns a list and nothing else.

context_only.reason: The restated Mindframe clause asks that the services named be matched to the content (a demographic group, a state, cultural diversity). That supports tailoring in general; it does not say which service suits which crisis category. The two remits G6 uses rest on service clauses of narrower or different scope than the categories: Kids Helpline's clause covers those aged 5 to 25 (children and young people), while the child_danger terms are usually said by an adult about a child, and 1800RESPECT's clause is about domestic or family violence, narrower than harmed_by_someone ('hits me', 'hurts me'). I found that the held healthdirect page also says Kids Helpline counsels parents of children in that age range, which supports the adult speaker, but the directory's clause does not carry it. Each remit's clause_says text does sit inside its entry's clause (I checked both).

The held form (pypdf text) prints under its seven rows only a coding line with three blanks for four columns and a total label, with no statement that the total is the sum of the seven item scores and no range. The sum is the standard reading, which I derive rather than read.

The WHO sentence (PDF page 8) is advice to the media: stories of people who got through a crisis are linked with fewer deaths, so such stories should be foregrounded. The response gives one generic line, that people do come through times like this, which is not a story and is not what the sentence asks for; the sentence does not say a one-to-one reply should assert it. The step from the clause to the line is G6's reading.

The restated Mindframe statement says discussion of self-harm should apply the guidance and the media's own codes so that audiences come to as little harm as possible. On the page it is a one-line summary pointing to a separate self-harm page, and the restatement's 'the guidelines ask' makes it sound like the guidelines page's own directive. It is a broad principle; the rule picks one concrete way (a single closed vocabulary for every category) and applies it to all five trigger categories, including harm to others, a child in danger and someone being harmed, which the statement does not mention.

The WHO sentence (PDF page 16) concerns media reporting stories of people who supported others in crisis. The rule is a different act: telling someone with concern for another person that they may use the same services. The held service pages do support it for most of the services named (Lifeline's page has a route for someone concerned about another person, the 988 page has a section for supporting a friend or relative, the Samaritans site has a page for that case, Suicide Call Back and Beyond Blue cover someone you know or a loved one, and the healthdirect page says Kids Helpline counsels parents), but the register's clauses do not carry those statements, so the clause reaches the rule only by context.

The held form (pypdf text) prints under its nine rows only an empty coding line, with a literal 0 for the first column and three blanks, ending in a blank for the total. It does not say in words to add the nine item scores, and it prints no range. That the total is the sum of nine item scores is the standard reading of the column-subtotal line, which I derive rather than read.

gad7_total.bounds: Answer lists for the PHQ-9 (nine items) and the GAD-7 (seven items): every item 0 to 3, the PHQ-9's item 9 mostly 0 and otherwise any value of the scale; one item with no answer, or one answer short; one answer off the scale (4, 5, 7 or -1); one answer too many; three inputs in four also raise one answered item by one. Boundary inputs: an off-scale item 9, a raise that takes item 9 from 0 to 1, a raise past 3, nine answers for the GAD-7 and ten for the PHQ-9, and no answers at all.

not_checked: Issuer state qualified-draft: these checks were frozen after the code they check existed (a retrofit), so by the issuer's freeze rule they can reach qualified-draft at most. A named gap holds it at qualified-draft at most: the independent reader attested that a clause supports its rule only by its context (read by context only: category_fit, gad7_total, hope, minimise_harm, others_too, phq9_total). A named gap holds it at qualified-draft at most: these guards have no threshold G6 can move (no comparison or number in their code), so only removing each one tests its cases: category_fit, crisis_lock, emergency_first, help_first, hope, language, licence_settled, method_location, minimise_harm, no_method, no_sensational_language, online_service, others_too, seek_help_message, where_and_how. A second route and invariants check these rules, and no value their source prints, by the independent reader's attestation (property-checked, no printed value: gad7_total, phq9_total).
No signed clinical or mental-health review is supplied: no qualified person has reviewed the listed terms, the exceptions, the response's words or which line fits which category.

The crisis trigger finds only its listed terms, as whole words after folding. Paraphrase, slang, other languages, misspellings beyond what folding undoes, look-alike letters Unicode NFKC does not fold, meaning without the listed words, and a self-harm act stated without the listed words are missed (the skill's 'Still missed' line). Finding no listed words is never evidence that a person is all right.

harmed_by_someone's terms fire on four known false positives ('hits me', 'is hitting me', 'hurts me' and 'is hurting me' in everyday sentences), kept on purpose; the other categories' known false positives are listed in crisis_rules.json and are not checked here.

Which line fits which category (Kids Helpline for a child in danger, 1800RESPECT for someone harmed by another person) rests on each line's own clause; no qualified person has checked that fit, and no other fit is checked.

The directory's numbers are checked against the held pages as of their retrieval dates (22 and 23 October 2026) only, not against the services as they are now. The NHS page was already past its own review date (3 February 2026) when it was retrieved, so every United Kingdom response carries the line saying the numbers may have changed.
No online support service is held for the United Kingdom (the register's missing entry), so its response names none.
A score is 'score computed', the sum of the item scores and nothing more: no severity band, risk level or diagnosis is given or checked.
An instrument whose licence entry is not settled (PCL-5, AUDIT, DASS-21, K10, MUST and the Barthel Index) stays refused; the terms of those licences are not checked here.
Each guard's cases check only whether it fired (effect_only): what else its code does rests on the independent reader's word.

crisis_lock, emergency_first, online_service, category_fit, licence_settled and the ten response checks hold no comparison or number for G6 to seed a boundary defect into, so each is checked by its cases and G6's removal of it only, and the record names it as the gap no_threshold.
The block's raw item-9 pre-check (block.py's _item_9_is_zero, run before typed validation) is a second path to the crisis result that to_a_person does not cover; no case here reaches it.

no_sensational_language and no_method are proxies. The first reads only an exclamation mark and the words 'suicide' and 'suicidal' as whole words in the response's own words (so a plural such as 'suicides' is not read by it; method_location's closed vocabulary is what keeps such a word out of a composed response). The second reads only the trigger's listed terms and the category names.

The response checks read what a composed response holds; this grounding cannot catch an omission. A response that named no service for a region the directory covers would pass where_and_how (no service line to fault) and seek_help_message (which reads its sentence, not its numbers).

The response checks' cases change the response the code composes as each case's edit says (lines swapped, moved or dropped, a sentence dropped, a service line's hours or ways to reach it taken off, words added); responses composed some other way are not checked. method_location and minimise_harm are one function, outside_words, and their cases check it twice.
The crisis lock's cases engage locks directly; the block's own bookkeeping of runs and subjects (its in-memory locks, which ids it accepts, the order of its doors) is not checked here.

emergency_first's cases arrange the directory's own entries (the emergency number held second, the entries reversed, the emergency number left out) and read the order lookup gives; the response's first line is checked under help_first.
numbers_checked's threshold cases use dates before retrieval (3 and 4 February 2026), the one place where only the NHS page's own review date moves.

The PHQ-9 and GAD-7 totals are property-checked: the forms print no worked total, so the known cases are the case author's arithmetic. The highest PHQ-9 total given is 24, because an item 9 answer other than 0 gives the crisis result instead; an item 9 answer off the scale is read as the crisis result before any refusal (the case author's ruling). -1 and -2 are this certificate's encoding of a refusal and the crisis result.
The trigger also reads each field's name and a phrase split across two fields; no case here checks either.
The guidance on writing about suicide is written for media; G6 applies it to a one-to-one reply, and no case checks that reading.
The crisis lock is held in memory for each run and subject id the caller supplies, so a restart, or another process, clears it.
where_and_how and seek_help_message cannot fault the response for a region the directory does not cover: that response names no service and says only to contact a local crisis line.

no_method and no_sensational_language are weak proxies: they pass words such as 'suicides' or a stated method. They are acceptable only because the response is G6's fixed text, checked against a closed vocabulary (outside_words).

review.binding: SSH signature over the certificate's content digest (the record without its history positions), namespace g6-certificate; verified when given, never required to list

answers.rule: the answers are the person's, as given, one per item in the form's order

answers_required.rule: an item with no answer, or an answer that is not one of the form's values, refuses the score; nothing is assumed

category_fit.rule: where a held clause states a remit matching what fired, that line takes the second place (no qualified person has reviewed a remit)

crisis_lock.rule: once the crisis result is given for a subject in a run, every later op for that subject in that run gives it again; nothing releases it

crisis_trigger.rule: any listed term, matched as whole words in any field after g6.guards folds the text and outside every exception's own words, gives the crisis result

directory_age.rule: past 180 days since retrieval the directory says the numbers may have changed (the WHO resource asks that contact details be checked regularly; the 180 days are G6's own)

emergency_first.rule: the response and the directory put the emergency number first, as the government directory does

few_services.rule: the response names only a few services a region: the emergency number, two lines open at all hours and one online service; the full directory travels beside it (WHO asks for a limited number; the two are Mindframe's)

fields.rule: the text scanned is what the caller gives, every field of it

gad7_total.rule: the GAD-7 total is the sum of its seven item scores, as the form's office-coding line adds them; the form prints no worked value

help_first.rule: the response opens with where to get help now, the region's emergency number first; a composed response that does not is never returned

hope.rule: the response says that people do come through times like this; a composed response that does not is never returned

language.rule: the response uses no phrase the language guide marks problematic; a composed response holding one is never returned

licence_settled.rule: an instrument whose licence entry is not settled is refused and ships no item text

method_location.rule: the response gives no detail of any method or place: it uses only G6's own reviewed words and the directory's own; a composed response holding any other word is never returned

minimise_harm.rule: one response serves every category the trigger fires on (self-harm included), with no detail of any act: the same reviewed words for every category and nothing else; a composed response holding any other word is never returned

no_method.rule: the response describes no act and repeats nothing the person said, nor what the trigger called it: the trigger finds no listed term in its own words and it names no category; a composed response that does is never returned

no_sensational_language.rule: the response uses plain, calm words and presents nothing as a solution: no exclamation mark, and its own words never name suicide; a composed response that does is never returned

numbers_checked.rule: when the numbers shown may have changed (the directory past 180 days, or a source past its review), the response and the card say so in one plain line (WHO asks only that contact details be checked regularly; the 180 days and the 12-month review window are G6's own, and a page's own review date is the directory's data)

online_service.rule: one online service a region where the directory holds one with a source; otherwise the gap is said, and none is invented

others_too.rule: the response tells someone worried about another person that they can contact the services too; a composed response that does not is never returned

phq9_item9.rule: any PHQ-9 item 9 answer other than 0 gives the crisis result, whatever the total (the form sets no threshold: this one is G6's own)

phq9_total.rule: the PHQ-9 total is the sum of its nine item scores, as the form's office-coding line adds them; the form prints no worked value

seek_help_message.rule: the response says that talking to someone can help, and how to reach someone now; a composed response that does not is never returned

two_all_hours_services.rule: after the emergency number, two services open at all hours a region where the directory holds them, and fewer only when it holds fewer, saying so

where_and_how.rule: each service named says how to reach it (call or text, the number, or the address to chat at) and when; a composed response with a line that does not is never returned
